lesson.title: The TCP handshake survives a lost packet
lesson.goal: See the three messages that open a TCP connection, and how a timer and a retransmit recover when one is lost.

say: To open a connection, the client sends a SYN to the server. The server gets it.
The server answers with a SYN-ACK, but it is lost on the way.
No reply comes back, so the server's timer runs out. It sends the SYN-ACK again.
This time the client gets it and replies with an ACK, which the server receives. Now the connection is open and both sides can send data.
